title: Effective operators and finite information

based_on.title: Introduction to computability theory

based_on.title: Computability: Some unofficial notes

summary: Characterize extensional computable transformations of programs by jointly enumerable rules using only finite positive observations.
abstract: An algorithm can take a program and produce another program. Suppose the resulting programs always have identical behavior whenever the original programs compute the same partial function, even if their texts differ. Each returned output is then forced by finitely many observed input–output pairs. One enumerable family of rules captures all these finite observations together, and a fixed compiler turns the rules back into programs. The rules also determine an action on partial functions that have no program at all. Myhill–Shepherdson shows that this finite-information extension is unique. Examples distinguish accepting either of two successful computations from waiting for one chosen call, and distinguish positive observations from a membership oracle that can report a pair absent from the entire graph.
